title: Two-step plain-autokey chains at lags 19-22 on one fully hidden alphabet (plain, cipher and fed letter), 4 sign forms, look-back and look-ahead: every cell decided exactly
k4_result: 32 cells (4 lags x back/ahead x 4 sign forms), 9-11 constant-free equations each. 18 are impossible (two letters forced into the same place), 14 are possible (a witness alphabet with 26 distinct places was found and re-checked by running the cipher through the chains), 0 undecided. The 18 impossible are exactly the 18 of idea 117; the 14 that idea 117 left undecided are all possible. All 4 lags have a possible cell; lag 20 look-back is impossible in all 4 forms. Possible cells per lag: 19: 4, 20: 2, 21: 3, 22: 5. By form: C = P - K and C = K - P 13 of 16 possible, C = P + K and C = -P - K 1 of 16 (lag 22 ahead, P + K). No reading of K4: a possible cell still leaves 15-17 free dimensions for the alphabet.
controls: 50 shuffled K4s, same 32 cells: possible 9-22 (median 16), impossible 10-23 (median 16), undecided 0. K4's 14 possible is lower than 38 controls, equal to 4, higher than 8. All 4 lags have a possible cell in 50 of 50 controls. Same-sign forms possible: 0-8, median 3 (K4 1; 11 controls at or below K4). Opposite-sign forms: 8-16, median 13 (K4 13). K4 is ordinary.
planted: 160/160: 5 English texts with the clue words in place for each lag 19-22 x back/ahead x 4 forms, random hidden alphabet and constant. Each reads back, the true alphabet satisfies the equations (with its constant, and moved along by E without one), and the true cell is decided possible with a verified witness. The other 31 cells of a planted text are impossible 8-22 times (median 15): a wrong cell dies about half the time.
scope_limits: One alphabet numbers plain, cipher and fed letter; fed letter = plaintext exactly d back or ahead, d = 19-22 (15-18 and 23-26 as an extra table: K4 4-8 of 8 possible per lag, inside the control range); coefficients +-1 only; clue blocks in place (clue 2 not moved). 'Possible' means the 24 clue letters cannot rule the cell out, nothing more: the test has no power to pick a true lag, since about half of all wrong cells also pass. No alphabet search and no English reading was attempted. Fed letter on a different numbering, a keyword on top, and cipher feed are not covered (ideas 136, 117).

negative.hypothesis: The two-step clue chains of a plain autokey at lag 19-22 on one hidden alphabet either rule the lag out or single K4 out from shuffled text.
negative.scope: X[C] = aX[P] + bX[K] + E, a, b = +-1, K = plaintext 19-22 back or ahead, one hidden alphabet on all three sides; 32 cells, each 9-11 linear equations mod 26 with distinct places required; decided exactly by forced-collision proof or verified witness.
negative.outcome: No signal: 18 of 32 cells impossible (same 18 as idea 117), the 14 undecided cells of idea 117 are all possible, so lags 19-22 stay open on a hidden alphabet (lag 20 look-back dead in all forms; P + K and -P - K dead except lag 22 ahead P + K). Controls: 50 shuffled K4s have 9-22 possible cells (median 16; K4 14), all 4 lags possible in 50/50. Planted 160/160 true cells possible with the true alphabet fitting; a wrong cell dies 50% of the time.

follow_ups: Read the 14 surviving cells: at lags 19-22 a full alphabet fixes 65-75 of the 97 letters (41-51 outside the clues) and the chains leave 15-17 free dimensions. Hill-climb the alphabet inside the chain solution space (keep the 9-11 equations exact, move the free letters) and score the fixed letters on the big quadgram model; first show a planted lag-21 text is recovered, since about 41 free letters against about 70 bits of alphabet freedom is near the limit.

The constant never matters when one hidden alphabet numbers all three letters: moving the alphabet along absorbs E in all four sign forms (for C = -P - K by E/3). Any later hidden-alphabet test can set E = 0 and save a factor of 26.
